newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: CRICKET-INDIAN TEAM NOT B-GRADE, SAYS TENDULKAR.
newsitem.headline: CRICKET-INDIAN TEAM NOT B-GRADE, SAYS TENDULKAR.

text.p: Indian cricket captain Sachin Tendulkar said on Sunday he was happy with his team in the four-nation Asian Cup and was confident they would win the one-day tournament.
Tendulkar denied a report in the Calcutta-based Bengali language daily Aajkal on Wednesday that he had said the team was sub-standard.
"I never made a statement it was a B-grade team," he told a news conference. "I am happy with it."
India's chief selector Ramakant Desai conceded on Friday that there were differences of opinion with Tendulkar after rumours that the 24-year-old Indian captain wanted another team.
But Tendulkar said any past disputes should be left behind.
"Whatever has happened, I am going to play a good tour and to play a good game and you have to be in a good frame of mind and leave things behind," he said.
Asked by reporters if he thought he would be able to win with the team as selected, Tendulkar replied: "Yes, I think so -- otherwise we would not have been here to play in Sri Lanka."
Tendulkar said he was delighted to have former Indian captain Mohammed Azharuddin back in the team.
"I think he is a great player. His performance says it all and his experience will help us a lot. We are very happy to have him included in the side."
Hosts and current world champions Sri Lanka will start the Asian Cup on Monday when they take on Pakistan at Colombo's R. Premadasa Stadium.
Bangladesh are the other team in the tournament, which concludes on July 26.
